verdict.rationale: Warp's own marketing describes background jobs that run on a recurring schedule or on event triggers. Defaults are enabled and users can write their own, and Warp Agent autonomously handles onboarding, payroll, tax notices and benefits while logging every action. The evidence comes only from the marketing homepage; there are no in-depth docs on how custom automations are authored or configured. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of authoring and managing custom scheduled or triggered jobs, details on the agent's autonomy controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Jobs that run on a schedule or when something happens. Defaults are on, and you can write your own.
Warp Agent takes onboarding, payroll, tax notices, and benefits. It asks when a decision is yours, and records every action it takes.
